reports.title: Financial Statements of the Government of the Cook Islands
reports.publisher: Ministry of Finance and Economic Management (MFEM), Cook Islands
reports.description: The audited whole-of-government financial statements of the Cook Islands, prepared by the Treasury under the Ministry of Finance and Economic Management Act 1995-96. Reports on IPSAS and cites individual standards by number (IPSAS 17, 21, 35, 36, 39, 40 all appear). Audited by the Cook Islands' own Audit Office under the Public Expenditure Review Committee and Audit (PERCA) Act 1995-96 — not by New Zealand, unlike Niue and Tokelau. SEVERE ARREARS: the most recent full set located this session covers FY2018 and was signed by the Financial Secretary and audited by the Director of Audit on the same day, 30 November 2020 — a twenty-nine-month lag. `releases_per_year` records the statutory intent; the cadence note records the practice.
reports.cadence_note: Statutorily annual. In practice heavily lagged: the FY2018 statements were authorised for issue and audited on 30 November 2020. The 2018 audit opinion is qualified on four matters, including inability to confirm taxation revenue.

release_schedule.note: As of June 2026, the Cook Islands Government's audited consolidated financial statements are severely backlogged, so there is no fixed or computable 'next' release date. Per a June 2026 Climate Finance Capacity Support Programme (CFCSP) article, in 2024 the government was 5 years behind (most recent completed/audited accounts were for FY ending June 2019 -- consistent with the corpus's current url, which links to the '2018 Cook Islands Government Financial Statements Final B' edition). MFEM's Treasury Management Division, with an embedded CFCSP-funded Financial Reporting Specialist, completed and submitted FY2020-FY2022 consolidated IPSAS-compliant statements to the Cook Islands Audit Office (CIAO) for audit by April 2026, narrowing the arrears to 3 years behind (as of 3 April 2026). The FY2023 statements were in final consolidation stages and expected to be submitted to CIAO by June 2026, after which work on FY2024 and FY2025 would begin 'at a slower pace.' No publisher calendar or statutory-deadline text was found (the site only states statements must comply with the MFEM Act 1995-96, without a quotable numeric deadline), and given the multi-year catch-up program in progress, any single projected 'next' date would likely be stale or wrong within months. MFEM's own Annual Financial Reports listing (https://www.mfem.gov.ck/crown-financial-reporting) still shows 2019 as the most recent published edition as of this research (11 Aug 2026), corroborating the backlog.

reports.title: Cook Islands Government Budget Estimates
reports.publisher: Ministry of Finance and Economic Management (MFEM), Cook Islands
reports.description: The annual appropriation estimates and commentary, Book 1. Punctual where the audited statements are not — the 2026/27 edition is dated May 2026, with the Minister's Statement of Responsibility dated Thursday 21 May 2026. Contains the economic forecasts, a forecasting model built with Asian Development Bank technical assistance, and an explicit statement that the fiscal information follows the IMF's Government Finance Statistics Manual 2014.

release_schedule.note: No published release calendar or explicit statutory deadline date was found on MFEM's or Parliament's site. However, multiple years show a consistent pattern: the Budget Estimates (Book 1/Book 2) are finalized and tabled in Parliament in May, ahead of the Cook Islands fiscal year start of 1 July, with parliamentary debate/passage sometimes extending into June (e.g. the FY2022/23 Budget Book 1 PDF is dated 17 May 2022 per its filename '...FINAL-20220517...'; a Public Accounts Committee 'Budget Review 2024-2025' report is dated 10 June 2024, implying the budget itself was tabled earlier that May; multiple Cook Islands News/RNZ articles on the '2025/26' and '2026/27' National Budgets appeared in the May-June window of 2025 and 2026 respectively). As of 2026-08-11, the FY2026/27 Budget has already been passed (RNZ: 'Cook Islands: $3 million boost for social welfare in record 2026/27 National Budget'; Cook Islands News: 'Parliament approves massive $375m budget'), so the next edition expected is the FY2027/28 Budget Estimates, projected for around May 2027 based on the observed pattern. Could not fetch MFEM/Parliament pages directly this session (WebFetch tool was rate-limited), so this is based on WebSearch result titles/snippets and known document filenames rather than a directly-read calendar page.

reports.title: Cook Islands Government Half-Year Economic and Fiscal Update
reports.publisher: Ministry of Finance and Economic Management (MFEM), Cook Islands
reports.description: The mid-year fiscal and economic update, structurally the Cook Islands analog of New Zealand's own HYEFU (`nz-treasury-befu`'s December counterpart). Carries its own Accounting Policies chapter for the forecast financial statements, whose Statement of Compliance names the IPSASB and — unusually candidly — points at a list of IPSAS standards the Government does not yet comply with.
reports.cadence_note: Annual, published in December: the 2023/24 edition is dated 14 December 2023 and the 2024/25 edition 10 December 2024.

entries.covers: 2026/27 Half-Year Economic and Fiscal Update (projected next release)

release_schedule.note: MFEM's National Budget archive page lists HYEFU editions released 24 Dec 2021, 15 Dec 2023, 13 Dec 2024, and 15 Dec 2025 (with 2020/21-2023/24 and 2019/20-2022/23 editions also listed but undated on the page). No statute or publisher rule stating an exact deadline was found; the pattern is a consistent mid-December release, roughly 6 months into the July-June fiscal year, so the 2026/27 edition is projected for mid-December 2026 (exact day not yet published as of 2026-08-11).

reports.title: National Accounts — Annual (Gross Domestic Product)
reports.description: The Cook Islands' annual GDP release, compiled mainly from VAT data on the production approach. Names SNA 2008 as its conceptual framework. NOTE THE INTERNAL CONFLICT this node resolves: the Statistics Office's own 'National Classifications' methodology page still describes the national accounts as 'largely based on' SNA68 with a series published 'from the year 1982-2001', while this release names SNA 2008 and carries data to 2024. Both are live on the same site. The methodology page is treated as stale and the release as current — see this slice's `_dropped` array, where the conflict is recorded rather than silently resolved.
reports.cadence_note: Annual release (the 2024 edition published 31 December 2025); quarterly GDP is also produced and is what the Budget forecasts from.

release_schedule.note: From the Cook Islands Ministry of Finance and Economic Management '2025-2026 Statistics Publication Calendar' PDF, which lists National Accounts (annual GDP by sector/industry) target release dates by reference calendar year: CY2025 -> May 2026, CY2026 -> May 2027 (the calendar explicitly states these are target dates and actual releases may occur before or after). As of today (2026-08-11) the National Accounts landing page (https://stats.gov.ck/national-accounts/) still shows 2024 as the latest completed annual edition (released 2025-12-31 per the 2024 report page), so the CY2025 annual report (targeted May 2026) appears overdue/delayed but not yet superseded by a later scheduled entry; it is kept as the first (soonest) entry rather than skipped, since it has not actually been published yet.

reports.title: National Accounts — Quarterly (Gross Domestic Product)
reports.publisher: Cook Islands Statistics Office (Ministry of Finance and Economic Management)
reports.description: The quarterly GDP release, split out from `ck-national-accounts` on 2026-08-06 because the Budget's forecasting model takes the quarterly series and not the annual one. Published roughly two to three quarters in arrears — the September quarter 2025 release is dated 18 June 2026. Compiled on the production approach at constant 2016 prices. Note that the Cook Islands Statistics Office attaches an identical 'More information on National Accounts' methodology block to both the quarterly and the annual release page, and that block is written for the quarterly series; see `_dropped`.
reports.cadence_note: Four releases a year, each roughly eight to nine months after the quarter it reports. The annual release is a separate publication on the same programme, dated 31 December 2025 for reference year 2024.

entries.covers: March Quarter 2025 and June Quarter 2025 GDP (both released together)
September Quarter 2025 and December Quarter 2025 GDP (both released together)
March Quarter 2026 and June Quarter 2026 GDP (projected next batch release)

release_schedule.note: No release calendar with future dates and no stated rule were found; the publisher's own '2025-26 Publication and Dissemination Calendar' PDF (https://stats.gov.ck/download/54/resources/6939/2025-26-publication-and-dissemination-calendar.pdf) lists nominal quarterly target months (Jul 2025, Oct 2025, Jan 2026, Apr 2026) but these targets are explicitly caveated ('reports may be released prior to or after the dates stated') and were badly missed in practice. Actual observed behavior on the site is that reports are published in twice-yearly catch-up batches (two quarters at a time), roughly ~5.5 months apart (2025-12-31 then 2026-06-18). Projected next batch (~Dec 2026, covering March & June Quarter 2026) is an extrapolation from only two observed data points and should be treated as low-precision.

reports.title: Cook Islands Consumer Price Index
reports.description: Quarterly consumer price index covering households on Rarotonga only, base year 2005, 205 priced items, weighted from the 2005 Household Income and Expenditure Survey and computed on the Laspeyres formula. NEGATIVE FINDING recorded on the node: the Statistics Office's own methodology text names the HIES as its weighting source but names NO external methodology manual — the IMF/ILO Consumer Price Index Manual (`cpi-manual`, already in this corpus) is not cited, unlike the SNA 2008 citation the national accounts carry.

release_schedule.note: No published release calendar found on the Cook Islands Statistics Office site. Publication is quarterly (matches releases_per_year=4 on file) but timing within each quarter varies: March-quarter CPI has been released Apr 4 2024, May 14 2025, and May 28 2026; June-quarter CPI released Aug 26 2024 and Aug 1 2025; September-quarter CPI released Nov 5 2024 and Nov 27 2025; December-quarter CPI released Feb 15 2024, Feb 14 2025, and Feb 25 2026. As of 2026-08-11 (today), the most recent published edition was March Quarter 2026 (released 2026-05-28); the June Quarter 2026 edition was not yet posted, so it is projected for August 2026 based on the prior two years' pattern.

reports.title: Government of Niue Consolidated Financial Statements
reports.description: Niue's whole-of-government consolidated financial statements. THE MOST STRUCTURALLY UNUSUAL NODE IN THIS SLICE: its Statement of Compliance names no external accounting framework at all, defining compliance by reference to the Government's own policies plus the Constitution of Niue and the Public Revenues Act 1959. Verified by grep over the full text of two separate sets — FY2023/FY2024 (26pp) and the five-year FY2017-21 document (37pp): zero occurrences of 'IPSAS', 'International Public Sector', 'XRB', 'New Zealand GAAP' or 'generally accepted accounting' in either. Niue has therefore never named an external standard back to FY2016 at least, which makes this a settled practice rather than an omission. Audited by the Controller and Auditor-General of New Zealand under Article 60 of the Constitution of Niue — so Niue imports New Zealand's auditor while importing nobody's accounting standards.
reports.cadence_note: Nominally annual and in severe arrears until recently. FY2017-21 were reported as a SINGLE five-year document under the Public Revenues (Financial Reporting and Audit Special Provisions) Amendment Act 2022, a statute passed specifically to permit it. FY2023 was authorised for issue on 19 May 2025 and FY2024 on 22 May 2025 — two years of accounts signed three days apart.

release_schedule.note: Niue's Government of Niue Consolidated Financial Statements (fiscal year ends 30 June) have a long documented history of severe, inconsistent delay rather than a fixed annual cycle. A 2011 PEFA assessment already noted a multi-year backlog (latest audited statements at the time were for FY2007/08, with FY2008/09 and FY2009/10 not expected complete until mid-2012). As of 2025, the government paid Deloitte New Zealand roughly NZD 2 million to clear the backlog: the FY2023 (year ended 30 June 2023) consolidated statements were only published 20 June 2025 (~24 months after fiscal year-end), and the FY2024 (year ended 30 June 2024) statements were published in September 2025 (~14 months after fiscal year-end) — lags that vary too much to project a consistent 'time of year'. The Auditor-General publicly stated that maintaining timely ANNUAL reporting going forward is 'critical', expressing an aspiration rather than a codified rule with a specific deadline; no statute, regulation, or publisher-stated numeric deadline (e.g. 'within N months of fiscal year end') could be found. As of 2026-08-11, no FY2025 (year ended 30 June 2025) consolidated financial statements have yet been posted on mof.gov.nu. Given the chronic historical irregularity and absence of any stated rule or calendar, this is best treated as irregular rather than assigning a fabricated 'next' date.

reports.title: Report to the Assembly, Government of Niue (Controller and Auditor-General of New Zealand)
reports.publisher: Controller and Auditor-General of New Zealand
reports.description: The New Zealand Auditor-General's periodic report to the Niue Assembly on the audits of the Government of Niue and its State-Owned Entities. Published by a New Zealand office about a Niue government, under Niue's own constitutional appointment — one of the few documents in this corpus whose publisher and subject are in different countries by constitutional design rather than by choice. The most recent edition covers three financial years at once and describes the backlog it was clearing.
reports.cadence_note: Irregular, driven by the audit backlog rather than a schedule: the edition read this session covers the years ended 30 June 2022, 2023 and 2024 together and is dated 19 May 2025.

release_schedule.note: No release calendar or statutory deadline found. The 22J/23J/24J combined report (dated 19 May 2025, published 20 June 2025) closed a multi-year audit backlog with help from Deloitte NZ (~NZ$2m spent). The Auditor-General has stated an intent to keep future reporting timely/annual going forward (tvniue, 11 Jul 2025), but no calendar, statute, or fixed rule specifying exact release dates was found on oag.parliament.nz or mof.gov.nu, and no numbered pattern of releases at consistent times of year exists yet given the backlog history. This is consistent with the existing cadence_note.

reports.title: Public Revenues Act 1959 (Niue)
reports.description: Niue's public finance statute, originally the Public Revenues Ordinance 1959. Section 25 requires the annual accounts to be furnished, audited and presented to the Assembly; section 40 requires a statement of public moneys and investments. NEGATIVE FINDING: neither section names an accounting basis or a standard. Together with the Constitution's Articles 58-60 this is the whole of the legal specification of Niue's public accounts — it fixes who prepares them, who audits them and who receives them, and says nothing about how they are measured. That silence is what leaves `nu-government-financial-statements` free to define its own compliance.
reports.cadence_note: A consolidated statute, reprinted on amendment rather than published on a schedule.

release_schedule.note: This is a one-off/foundational legal instrument (an Act of the Niue Assembly governing public revenue administration), not a recurring statistical or administrative report. It is amended or reprinted irregularly as Niue's legislature sees fit (e.g. consolidated in periodic 'Niue Laws' compilations such as the 2006 edition), not on any fixed schedule. No release calendar, stated periodicity rule, or consistent-interval pattern of amendment/reissue was found on PacLII, gov.nu, or WIPO Lex. The releases_per_year=1 field on file appears to misclassify this as a recurring periodical; it should probably not carry a fixed cadence at all.

reports.title: Financial Statements of the Government of Tokelau
reports.description: The annual financial statements required by Rule 9 of the Tokelau Finance Rules 1998, prepared for the General Fono and audited by the Controller and Auditor-General of New Zealand. CADENCE WARNING, and it is severe: the most recent publicly located instance covers FY2004 and reached this corpus through a New Zealand parliamentary paper (the Administrator of Tokelau's report, E.14), not through a Tokelau publication channel. This node rests on a live statutory requirement plus a twenty-two-year-old published instance. Treat its currency as unestablished until a future session finds a recent set — see this slice's `_dropped` array.
reports.cadence_note: Rule 9 requires preparation 'no later than 1 September in every year'. The most recent instance this session could locate covers the year ended 30 June 2004, published inside a New Zealand parliamentary paper.

entries.covers: Financial statements for the year ended 30 June 2026

release_schedule.rule: Rule 9 of the Tokelau Finance Rules 1998 requires the financial statements of the Government of Tokelau to be prepared no later than 1 September in every year.
release_schedule.note: Independently corroborated via the primary source PDF at the corpus's existing url (a NZ parliamentary paper, 'Report of the Administrator of Tokelau for the period ended 30 June 2006'), whose audit opinions for FY2002-FY2004 each cite preparation 'pursuant to Rule 9 of the Tokelau Finance Rules 1998.' Could not independently re-locate the primary text of the Tokelau Finance Rules 1998 itself (paclii.org, the main Pacific legislation repository, returned HTTP 403 to both WebFetch and direct curl through the proxy on every attempt), so the exact '1 September' wording relies on the pre-existing cadence_note rather than a freshly fetched rule text. No evidence was found of any financial statements published for a fiscal year after 30 June 2004 being publicly available — Tokelau Administration's own site (tokelau.org.nz) does not host a financial-statements release calendar or archive; only Trust Fund annual reports and sector reports were listed there.

reports.title: Tokelau Finance Rules 1998
reports.description: Tokelau's public finance rules. Requires annual financial statements prepared 'in accordance with generally accepted accounting practice' — WITHOUT SAYING WHOSE, which is the third distinct answer the Realm gives to the same question (Cook Islands names IPSAS; Niue names nothing and says so; Tokelau names an undefined GAAP). Separately installs the Auditor-General of New Zealand as auditor and requires every auditor in Tokelau to be qualified to act as an auditor in New Zealand.

release_schedule.note: The Tokelau Finance Rules 1998 is a foundational legal instrument made by the General Fono (Tokelau's national legislative body), not a recurring statistical publication. PacLII's chronological table of General Fono Rules (paclii.austlii.edu.au/tk/indices/legis/rules-by-year.html) shows the original 1998 Finance rule followed by amendments in 2004 ('Finance Amendment'), 2006 ('Finance Amendment [Public Money]'), and 2015 ('Finance Amendment Rules') -- gaps of 6, 2, and 9 years respectively, with no stated periodicity. No General Fono or PacLII page describes a review calendar or fixed amendment cycle for these Rules; amendments occur whenever the General Fono decides to legislate on finance matters. This should not be treated as having a fixed release cadence.

relations.basis: VERIFIED DIRECTLY by the minting session (Report to the Assembly and the FY2024 consolidated statements, both fetched from mof.gov.nu with plain curl and pypdf-extracted); converted from a `_dropped` note to a `Relation` on 2026-08-06 when the schema question was decided. EXPORT OF INSTITUTION, and the appointment runs the unexpected way. The FY2024 audit report is signed "John Ryan / Controller and Auditor-General / Wellington, New Zealand", and his independence statement reads: "Other than in exercising functions and powers under Article 60 of the Constitution of Niue, I have no relationships with or interests in the Government of any of its subsidiaries." So a New Zealand statutory officer audits Niue's public accounts under NIUE'S OWN constitution, not under New Zealand law — Niue appoints the New Zealand Auditor-General, New Zealand does not impose him. The Report to the Assembly opens: "I am pleased to report that the financial statements and associated audits of the Government of Niue (the Government) and its State-Owned Entities (SOEs) for the years ended 30 June 2022, and 30 June 2023 have now been completed and the audit opinions issued." NOTE that this pair also carries a `uses_data_from` dependency in the same slice, and the duplication is correct rather than an error: the Auditor-General's report both takes the statements as its data and assures them, and only the first of those is a dependency. This is the corpus's first `Relation` and the pair was chosen partly because it demonstrates that a dependency and a relation over the same two nodes are different claims.

VERIFIED DIRECTLY by this session (2026-08-06, second thread) from two separate recurring publications of the Office of the Auditor-General, both read in a browser after oag.parliament.nz was found to redirect to a rebranded ao.parliament.nz. Annual report 2024/25, Part 1: About us: "The Auditor-General is also the Auditor-General of the governments of Niue and Tokelau, and the Secretary-General of the Pacific Association of Supreme Audit Institutions (PASAI), which works to strengthen supreme audit institutions throughout the Pacific." The Auditor-General's strategic intentions to 2031, Part 1: "The Auditor-General of New Zealand also serves as Auditor-General for the governments of Niue and Tokelau, and as Secretary-General of the Pacific Association of Supreme Audit Institutions (PASAI)." The receiving instrument was already verified by the minting session and is unchanged — Tokelau Finance Rules 1998: "(1) There shall be an auditor of accounts for the Tokelau Administration. (2) The Auditor-General of New Zealand shall be the auditor of accounts which contain public money, and, unless legislation otherwise directs, of each body corporate of Tokelau." CORRECTION TO THIS SLICE'S OWN FRAMING, established this session and recorded in NZ/G.4.md Corrections. The `_dropped` note that this relation replaces said Tokelau's auditor is installed "by an instrument of the Tokelau Administration, Niue's by Niue's own Constitution, and neither by New Zealand law". The last clause is wrong for Tokelau. "Tokelau Administration" is listed by name in Schedule 2 of the New Zealand Public Audit Act 2001, "Specific public entities not falling within any class", referenced to s 5(1)(d) — so Tokelau is a New Zealand public entity by New Zealand statute, and is audited on that footing as well as under its own Finance Rules. Niue appears nowhere in the Act: a full-text search of the current consolidation returns one occurrence of "Tokelau" and zero of "Niue". The contrast therefore survives but runs the OTHER WAY from how the note stated it. Niue is the pure export-of-institution case — New Zealand law is silent and Niue's own Constitution reaches out to appoint a New Zealand statutory officer. Tokelau is doubly installed, and one of the two instruments is New Zealand's own.
